business_problem: Shorthills AI needed to make legal research more comprehensive and trustworthy across very large corpora without forcing users to accept incomplete, hallucinated or weakly sourced answers.
solution_summary: Shorthills AI collaborated with IBM to build a production-grade legal search platform on IBM watsonx.data. The architecture combines hybrid retrieval methods—keyword, vector and graph-based search—behind a routing layer that sends each query to the most appropriate strategy. Documents are ingested into a secure data lake, chunked intelligently and enriched with entities such as judge names, case types and citations. Embeddings are stored in watsonx.data so the system can perform semantic retrieval at scale, while Langflow helps compose the modular search workflow. The platform then reranks results and returns citation-backed answers rather than partial or opaque outputs. By treating search as a governed, multi-method retrieval problem rather than a simple chatbot prompt, Shorthills built a secure, on-premises-capable legal-research engine that improves recall, comprehensiveness and the diversity of legal reasoning for enterprise clients.
